title: Rung 2 -- two triangles sharing an edge, and the shared edge is not a seam

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- rung 2 of the ten scenes: one quad rotated off both axes, so depth varies across the frame

acceptanceClass.because: A 1.5 x 1.0 m rectangle, fronto-parallel, rolled by -arctan(1/2) so all four edges take slope -1/2 or 2, and scaled so that both parallel pairs are separated by a whole number of lattice steps while the frame's own centre puts each pair at half a step (`board/`). The rational aspect 3:2 is what makes two separation conditions solvable with one scale freedom; the four corners land on exact half-pixel raster coordinates and the margin is 0.223606797749979 px on every edge, 45 times the oracle's own 0.005 px filter half-width.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: THE EXACTNESS CONSTRUCTION OF `board/`, AND NOT I.26.10'S FRAMING RULE -- the two are separate determinations of the camera distance and a case carries exactly one. FRONTO-PARALLEL: the subject is a 1.5 x 1.0 m rectangle in the plane z = 0 and the eye sits on that plane's own normal through its centre, so the perspective image is a SIMILARITY and the raster slopes are the subject's own, rotated by the roll and by nothing else. ROLL -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg carries world +X to raster (2,-1)/sqrt5 and world +Y to (-1,-2)/sqrt5, so the four edges are two lines -1x-2y=c and two lines 2x-1y=c, all with |n| = sqrt5 and a margin ceiling of 0.223606797749979 px. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. SCALE: writing u = k*sqrt5 for k px per metre at the plane's depth, the two constants of each parallel pair differ by 1.0*u and by 1.5*u, so half-lattice on all four needs both to be even integers -- u = 0 (mod 4). The frame decides which one: the rotated bounding box is 0.8u x 0.7u px, so 0.7u <= 720 admits u = 1020 with 3.5 px of vertical slack, and that slack is the only reason for 1020 rather than 1024. k = 1020/sqrt5 = 456.15786564927665 px per metre and the depth at which one metre subtends k px is (720/2)/(0.24*k) = 3.288335261029103 m. AIM: the subject's own centre, and no nudge at all. The frame's centre pixel is (639.5, 359.5), so p*639.5 - q*359.5 = (1279p - 719q)/2 is at half a lattice step whenever p + q is odd, which both (-1,2) and (2,1) are; and each pair's constants sit half a separation either side of it, at u/2 = 510 and 1.5u/2 = 765, both whole. The four corners land on exact half-pixel raster coordinates -- (435.5, 716.5), (1047.5, 410.5), (231.5, 308.5), (843.5, 2.5) -- so every pixel in the frame is unambiguously inside or outside. THE CLAIM IS RECOMPUTED, NOT TRUSTED: the runner measures both conditions from the projected geometry and refuses this class if either fails. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) and the clip range [0.1, 100] m are Blender's factory camera, measured from a --factory-startup scene: lens 50 mm, sensor height 24 mm, clip_start 0.1 m, clip_end 100 m.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Diffuse BSDF with Roughness pinned to 0, never Principled: Principled at metallic 0 still carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5. This subject is a single unoccluded facet, which is the one shape where Cycles has no integration left and the answer is the closed form rho*L = 0.8 x 0.05087608844041824 = 0.0407008707523346 -- so this is one of the cases that keeps that number exercised (board:0087).

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

notes: The one thing over rung 1: a second triangle, sharing an edge with the first. The shared edge must not show in the coverage mask at all -- a rasteriser that drops or doubles the pixels along a shared edge produces a one-pixel seam, and this is the cheapest subject that can show one.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices; exact because the subject is a plane perpendicular to the optical axis, so its perspective image is a similarity and the area is 1.5 m^2 * k^2 = 1.5 * u^2/5 = 312120 px^2 at u = 1020, which is 33.8671875 % of the frame and above the section's 30 % floor
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
